summary: Iteration 1 fixes substantively address 4 of the 5 critical-uncovered-paths flagged in r1. Specifically: (1) SSE parser is now hand-tracable against committed Tests/Fixtures/sse-anthropic-sample.txt during Task 9 Code Audit; (2) marker parser is hand-tracable against Tests/Fixtures/marker-cases/*.md during Task 9 and explicitly verified in Task 11 Test Audit; (3) ARC-leak risk is mitigated by promoting the Instruments Allocations check to Mandatory in Task 12 plus an explicit error-path trigger; (4) GraphRAG mapReduceForFolder now has all thresholds pinned in Decision 5 (30/50KB/200KB/500/30); (5) tab-switch-during-stream is addressed in Decision 11 §5 (stream continues, buffer accumulates, repaint from snapshot on switch-back). Decision 9 was amended to commit fixtures even without test code, and the follow-up task in tasks/todo.md now has owner (Boris), target date (2026-05-14), and additional test scopes (scope_hint validation, cancellation race, resource caps). Remaining gaps are not critical but should be acknowledged: the Instruments leak check is a single manual sample on a smoke session — it can miss leaks that only manifest on the failure/retry path or after deep tree expansion (only 2-3 levels are sampled); the tab-switch-during-stream prescription in Decision 11 §5 is not paired with an acceptance criterion or a manual verification step in user-spec, so it risks being unimplemented or untested at QA time; the fixtures themselves are not yet in tree (referenced as 'commit during Task 1/5'), so there is no mechanism to verify their content quality before implementation begins. Strategy is materially defensible for merge, contingent on these residual minor items being acknowledged or closed.

findings.location: Section: Decision 11 §5 (Tab switch during stream) and Acceptance Criteria
findings.issue: Decision 11 §5 prescribes tab-switch-during-stream behavior ('stream continues in the background; streamingBuffer keeps accumulating. When user switches back, JS re-renders from the current streamingBuffer snapshot. No re-stream, no data loss.') which directly addresses r1's bridge-message-replay concern. However, this prescription has no corresponding entry in the Acceptance Criteria section of tech-spec.md and no manual verification step in the Agent Verification Plan or user-spec 'Как проверить' section. Without an acceptance criterion or QA step, the implementer can ship without exercising this path, and Pre-deploy QA (Task 12) has no checklist item to verify it.
findings.recommendation: Add to tech-spec Acceptance Criteria under 'Lifecycle & memory': '[ ] Switching to another tab and back during a streaming insight node restores correct rendered state from session memory (no re-stream, no data loss); buffer accumulated during background continues to render on switch-back.' Add a corresponding manual step to Task 12's verification list: 'Open Recursive Insight, switch to another tab while stream is mid-progress, wait 5 seconds, switch back; confirm content rendered matches the buffer that accumulated during background and no LLM call was re-invoked (verify via network inspector or by counting Anthropic API call count).' Optionally add the same step to user-spec 'Как проверить → Пользователь проверяет'.

findings.location: Section: Task 12 Pre-deploy QA — Instruments Allocations leak check
findings.issue: The promoted Instruments leak check is now Mandatory and triggers an error path, which is a real improvement. But the prescribed sample is narrow: 'open insight tab, expand 2-3 deep-dives, close tab'. This will catch the bulk-case retain cycle (closure captures self in onDelta) but will miss two specific leak shapes that the spec explicitly creates risk for: (a) leak only manifests after a failed-then-retried node (Decision 11 §3 retryCurrent path replaces failed node content — if retry creates a new closure that holds the prior node, the prior node leaks); (b) leak only manifests after eviction (Decision 10 §7 evicts oldest non-current nodes — if evicted nodes are still referenced by a Task continuation or a JS-side cache, they leak silently). Neither path is exercised by 'expand 2-3 deep-dives then close tab'.
findings.recommendation: Expand Task 12 mandatory Instruments step to include two additional snapshot points: (1) trigger a stream failure (e.g., disconnect Wi-Fi mid-stream), confirm error banner, click Retry, let it succeed, then take an Allocations snapshot — verify no retained InsightNode for the failed-then-replaced node; (2) expand more than 5 deep-dives (or whatever count exceeds the 50 MB session cap with the test fixtures available) to trigger eviction, then take a snapshot — verify evicted InsightNode instances are actually freed, not just removed from the nodes dictionary. If 50 MB is hard to hit with TestFiles content, temporarily lower the cap during this QA step (note in spec).

findings.location: Section: Task 11 Test Audit — fixture content verification
findings.issue:
Task 11 (d) says test-master will verify 'committed fixtures are present, complete, and represent the documented edge cases'. This is correct in principle but the documented edge cases for marker-cases (happy, in-code-fence, as-hr, no-marker, multiple-markers) omit two cases that r1 explicitly flagged: (a) CRLF line endings (LLM may emit 
; marker requires 

 boundaries — CRLF will silently fail the boundary check and produce no deep-dive split), (b) partial marker mid-stream (marker text appears across two SSE chunks — JS receives '...---DEEP-' then '-DIVES---
'; debounced render at the wrong moment could render the partial as a horizontal rule then jump-replace it, causing flicker). Similarly the SSE fixture cases (happy path, partial chunks, ping comments, error event, oversized line) omit a case that r1 flagged: a `data:` line split across two `bytes` reads — the `URLSession.bytes(for:).lines` API will block until newline arrives, but if the parser is later refactored to use `.bytes` directly, this becomes a regression risk; locking the fixture now is cheap insurance.
findings.recommendation: Add to Task 5 fixture set: `Tests/Fixtures/marker-cases/crlf.md` (marker preceded by \r\n\r\n) and `Tests/Fixtures/marker-cases/partial-mid-stream.md` (split into two halves to simulate chunked arrival; documented as 'parser must not split on first half'). Add to Task 1 fixture set: a 6th example showing a `data: {long JSON containing escaped newline}` event split across two TCP-frame boundaries (simulated by inserting a literal split marker the test will use to feed the parser in two passes). These take ~10 minutes to author and lock parser behavior against the two specific edge cases that manual testing on real LLM output will not deterministically reproduce.

findings.issue: Follow-up scope was expanded with three additional tests (scope_hint validation, cancellation race, resource caps) — good coverage of r1 gaps. Two scopes still missing that the tech-spec explicitly creates risk for: (1) eviction correctness (Decision 10 §7: 'oldest non-current nodes are evicted' — needs a test that verifies evicted nodes are actually deallocated, not just removed from the nodes dictionary, and that the current navigation path is preserved), (2) retry-after-failure correctness (Decision 11 §3: retryCurrent re-runs the same prompt and 'replaces the failed node's content' — needs a test that verifies the failed node ID is preserved, the rawBuffer is reset, and no orphan InsightNode instance remains).
findings.recommendation: Append to tasks/todo.md follow-up task Item 5: 'Tests/InsightEvictionTests.swift — verify oldest-non-current-path nodes are deallocated on session-cap exceed, current navigation path preserved across eviction.' and 'Tests/InsightRetryTests.swift — verify retryCurrent replaces failed node content in place (same node ID), rawBuffer reset, lastError cleared on success, no orphan node instance remains in nodes dictionary or as ARC-retained closure capture.'

findings.issue: Decision 9 says 'fixture files committed now even without test code' and Tasks 1 and 5 enumerate the fixtures to commit. But the fixtures do not yet exist in /Users/boris/Documents/Claude/Projects/MarkDV/MarkView/Tests/Fixtures/ (verified: directory absent). They will be created during Task 1/5 implementation, which is the right time mechanically — but it means the Audit Wave (Task 9 Code Audit, Task 11 Test Audit) can only verify fixtures that the same waves' authors just produced. There is no independent third-party fixture authoring step. Risk: an implementer can produce fixtures that conveniently match their parser implementation rather than canonical Anthropic SSE / canonical marker edge cases. This is a structural review-quality concern, not a correctness concern.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add a pre-Task-1 mini-task: 'Author fixtures from canonical sources before parser implementation begins — capture SSE sample via real curl invocation against Anthropic API, hand-write marker cases against Decision 2 marker spec, commit before any parser code exists', so the parser is written to fit the fixtures rather than the other way round; or (b) add to Task 9 Code Audit description an explicit instruction: 'verify SSE fixture contents against Anthropic SSE specification (https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/messages-streaming), not against the parser's own behavior — flag any fixture that looks like it was authored to match the parser rather than the protocol'. Option (b) is cheaper and sufficient.

pyramidBalance.assessment: absent — no test target exists in project; deferred by explicit user decision (Decision 9). Iteration 1 fixes have substantially closed the compensating-verification gaps that r1 flagged: fixtures + hand-trace in Audit Wave covers SSE/marker; Mandatory Instruments check covers ARC; pinned thresholds in Decision 5 cover GraphRAG; Decision 11 §5 covers tab-switch. Remaining gaps are minor coverage misses, not critical voids.

iteration1FixesAssessment.fix1_fixtures_committed: Substantively addressed. Decision 9 now mandates fixture commit during Tasks 1 and 5; Task 9 Code Audit hand-traces against them; Task 11 Test Audit verifies their presence and edge-case representation. Residual minor gap: missing CRLF and partial-mid-stream marker cases, missing TCP-frame-split SSE case (see finding 3).
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix2_thresholds_pinned: Fully addressed. Decision 5 now lists 30 file folder cutoff, 50 KB per-file truncation, 200 KB per-community subdivision, 500 file hard cap, 30 file scope_hint cap. Acceptance Criteria mirror these. Closes r1's GraphRAG threshold concern.
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix3_instruments_mandatory: Mostly addressed. Task 12 explicitly says 'Mandatory: run Instruments → Allocations on a smoke session' and triggers an error path. Residual minor gap: sample is narrow — does not cover failed-then-retried leak shape or post-eviction leak shape (see finding 2).
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix4_smoke_multitoken: Fully addressed. Task 1 verify-smoke now uses 'count from 1 to 20 with brief explanation each' which produces multiple content_block_delta events across multiple TCP chunks, exercising the parser's chunk-reconstruction logic. Closes r1's concern that 'say hi' could fit in one packet and miss the parsing bug class.
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix5_followup_owned: Substantively addressed. tasks/todo.md now has Owner: Boris, target date 2026-05-14, and additional test scopes (scope_hint validation, cancellation race, resource caps). Residual minor gap: missing eviction correctness and retry-after-failure correctness tests (see finding 4).
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix6_task9_handtrace: Fully addressed. Task 9 description now explicitly states 'hand-trace SSE parser against Tests/Fixtures/sse-anthropic-sample.txt and marker parser against Tests/Fixtures/marker-cases/*.md'. Closes r1's concern that the Audit Wave had no concrete inputs to verify against.
iteration1FixesAssessment.fix7_task11_verifies_fixtures: Fully addressed. Task 11 description item (c) verifies fixtures present and representing documented edge cases; item (e) verifies Pre-deploy QA Instruments check is sufficient to catch ARC-cycle risk. Closes r1's concern that fixtures could be missing or insufficient.
iteration1FixesAssessment.tabSwitchCovered: Partially addressed. Decision 11 §5 prescribes the behavior, which is the substantive fix. But there is no acceptance criterion and no manual QA step for it (see finding 1).
iteration1FixesAssessment.remainingResidualRisk: Low. The remaining gaps are minor and limited to: tab-switch acceptance criterion missing, narrow Instruments sample, two missing fixture edge cases (CRLF, partial-mid-stream), two missing follow-up test scopes (eviction, retry), and a structural concern about fixture authoring sequence. None of these are likely to produce a build-blocking bug; they are 'leave one more layer of safety on the table' rather than 'critical path uncovered'.
